11:29 < jal0> andrye: was thinking of modifying the modules.c file of your to produce "command files".
11:30 < jal0> which is basically the information you already dump, just formatted in a different way
11:32 < andrey> sure, go ahead.
11:33 < andrey> command files for REC?
11:34 < jal0> btw, i finnaly figured out how to generate "physical addresses" realtime. which i not as straight forward as it may sound, you have to deal with the cache.
11:34 < jal0> yes
11:36 < andrey> what is "realtime"?
11:37 < jal0> i can say create a pointer to a string ( char* test= {"Hello World"} ) in my program and then find the physical memory where it is located while the program is running.
11:39 < jal0> it's alot different that just converting the linear address to physical address used with memory dumps, because you cannot be sure that any memory was actually written due to the cache.
11:41 < jal0> i basically had to create an interface to the undocumented CacheSync function provided by coredll.dll.
11:45 < jal0> the code for it is in ~jal0/Virt2Phys
11:45 < jal0> im not sure how to set permissions for the directory though in windows
11:48 < jal0> ok, i think i figured it out. if you have a chance can you see if you can access it?
12:02 < andrey> I can cd to ~jal0 but cannot do ls. But if I cd to ~jal0/Virt2Phys than I'm ok.
12:02 < jal0> hmm
12:03 < jal0> try now
12:03 < andrey> ls: .: Permission denied
12:04 < andrey> just do "chmod g+r"
12:04 < jal0> try again
12:04 < jal0> i'm using a windows GUI prog WinSCP
12:06 < andrey> what is the protocol? FTP?
12:06 < andrey> ok, works now
12:06 < jal0> SCP? not sure
12:08 < jal0> Virt2Phys.cpp is basically the code from you modules.c file, changes to used file mapping. in addition, it works with actual ram real time.
12:09 < andrey> ic. I'm looking into it now.
12:10 < jal0> i also tryed to add some more documentation :)
12:10 < andrey> btw if you determine physical address and then use 0x80000000+physAddr won't it go through cache?
12:10 < jal0> yes, i beleive, why
12:10 < andrey> comments? or separate file?
12:11 < andrey> It that case you don't need to commit cache before accessing.
12:11 < jal0> both
12:12 < jal0> actually you do if your creating variables on the stack as in the example program.
12:12 < jal0> the problem is not with converting the linear address, rather copying data from the RAM pointed to by the physical address
12:15 < jal0> when doing stuff "real time" accessing kernel data should be done through the cache, as it can be changed by windows. thats the reason for using KSEG0_BASE as _rambase.
12:16 < jal0> but when you need to actually access the physical memory, you have to make sure that the cache has been "written back"
12:18 < andrey> ic
12:18 < jal0> if you comment out the call to CacheSync(), you'll see the effects. the output is not always correct.
12:20 < jal0> i would also like to maybe add these headers to CVS, and add new stuff to them as we find it. most of the info use to create then was from the different versions of PB
12:22 < jal0> anyway, time to go to work :(. talk to you later
12:22 < andrey> Make sense.
12:22 < andrey> take care
